title: PriorityQueue: Min-Heaps & Priority Processing
summary: Master PriorityQueue: how an internal binary heap array guarantees O(1) peek and O(log N) insertion/removal based on natural ordering.
prerequisites: The Queue Contract & FIFO Buffer Processing
learningObjectives: Understand the complete binary min-heap data structure and array-based pointer-free representation
Master the mathematical indexing equations for parent and child nodes: (i-1)>>>1, 2i+1, 2i+2
Trace sift-up (offer) and sift-down (poll) rebalancing algorithms with O(log N) complexity
Diagnose the critical iteration order pitfall: why iterator() does not output sorted elements
expectedOutcomes: Confidence implementing heap-based scheduling and Dijkstra algorithms using PriorityQueue
Ability to articulate binary min-heap memory locality and iteration guarantees in technical interviews

activities.title: Practical Context: Hospital Emergency Room Triage Dispatch

analogy.headline: Practical Context: Hospital Emergency Room Triage Dispatch
analogy.story:
In an emergency trauma room, arriving patients are not treated in First-In, First-Out sequence. A patient with a minor headache who arrived at 8:00 AM does not precede a cardiac arrest patient who rushed in at 8:15 AM.

Instead, triage nurses assign clinical urgency scores: Severity 1 (Critical) immediately jumps ahead of Severity 4 (Non-urgent). When a new high-severity patient arrives, the triage roster dynamically adjusts (sift-up). The chief trauma surgeon always attends to the lowest severity-score patient currently at the top of the roster (O(1) peek, O(log N) poll).

This priority-governed dispatching is the exact real-world model of a PriorityQueue.
analogy.keyTakeaway: PriorityQueue orders elements by priority (min-heap by default), ensuring the highest-priority item is instantly accessible at the root in O(1) time.

activities.title: PriorityQueue Architecture: Binary Min-Heaps & Sift Mechanics

keyTakeaways: PriorityQueue is an unbounded priority queue based on a binary min-heap packed into a contiguous Object[] array
Parent at index i: parent = (i - 1) >>> 1; Children: left = 2*i + 1, right = 2*i + 2
offer() runs siftUp in O(log N) time; poll() runs siftDown in O(log N) time; peek() is O(1)
CRITICAL: Iterating via iterator() or for-each prints raw array heap order, NOT sorted priority order

activities.content:
### Definition of java.util.PriorityQueue

A **`java.util.PriorityQueue<E>`** is an unbounded priority queue based on a balanced binary min-heap. The elements of the priority queue are ordered according to their **natural ordering** (via `Comparable<E>`) or by a `Comparator<E>` provided at queue construction time.

By default, `PriorityQueue` is a **Min-Heap**: the head of the queue is the *least* element with respect to the specified ordering.

---

### Array Representation of Complete Binary Trees

Instead of allocating tree node objects with left/right object pointers, `PriorityQueue` maps the complete binary tree directly into a flat contiguous `Object[] queue` array:
* **Parent of index `i`**: `(i - 1) >>> 1` (integer division by 2)
* **Left Child of index `i`**: `2 * i + 1`
* **Right Child of index `i`**: `2 * i + 2`

**The Min-Heap Invariant**: For every node $i$ (except the root at index $0$):
$$\text{queue}[\text{parent}(i)] \le \text{queue}[i]$$

The root at index $0$ is guaranteed to be the minimum element, enabling **`peek()` in $O(1)$**.

---

### Rebalancing: Sift-Up vs Sift-Down

1. **`offer(E e)` — Sift-Up ($O(\log N)$)**:
   The new element is appended at the first open leaf (`queue[size]`). It is compared against its parent; if smaller, the parent shifts down and the element sifts up until the heap invariant is restored.
2. **`poll()` — Sift-Down ($O(\log N)$)**:
   The root at index $0$ is removed. The last element in the array (`queue[size - 1]`) moves to index $0$. It is compared against its smaller child; if larger, the smaller child shifts up and the element sifts down.

---

### The Iteration Order Trap

A universal beginner trap is expecting `for (int x : priorityQueue)` to print elements in sorted order. **It does not!**
The iterator visits elements in backing array order, which satisfies heap structural properties but is NOT sorted. To extract elements in true priority order, you must sequentially invoke **`poll()`** until the queue is empty.

---

### Executable Demonstration: Min-Heap Extraction vs Iteration

activities.title: Hospital Patient Triage Pipeline
activities.description: Trace an emergency medical triage processor ordering patients by clinical urgency score using PriorityQueue.

steps.description: Patient implements Comparable<Patient>, defining natural order by comparing urgencyScore ascending (1 is least numeric, highest priority).
Enqueue patients in arbitrary arrival order. Bob (P1) and Diana (P1) sift up to the top of the heap.
Sequential erQueue.poll() extracts Bob and Diana first, followed by Charlie (P2) and Alice (P3).

questions.question: What is the time complexity of peek(), offer(), and poll() on a PriorityQueue with N elements?
options: peek: O(1), offer: O(1), poll: O(N)
peek: O(1), offer: O(log N), poll: O(log N)
peek: O(log N), offer: O(log N), poll: O(1)
peek: O(N), offer: O(1), poll: O(1)
questions.explanation: peek() inspects queue[0] directly in O(1). offer() performs sift-up in O(log N), and poll() replaces root and performs sift-down in O(log N).

questions.question: What happens if you insert null into a PriorityQueue via queue.offer(null)?
options: It is placed at the root since null has value 0
It is silently ignored and returns false
It is placed at the tail of the heap
questions.explanation: PriorityQueue strictly forbids null elements. Because elements must be mutually comparable, invoking offer(null) throws NullPointerException immediately.

qaList.question: What happens if an object already stored inside a PriorityQueue has its comparison fields modified in-place?
qaList.answer: If an object's comparison key is mutated while inside a PriorityQueue, the heap invariant is silently corrupted. PriorityQueue has no change listeners or internal re-heapify triggers on object mutation. The mutated element remains in its original array index, violating the parent-child heap ordering. Subsequent poll() and peek() operations will return wrong elements or fail to find expected items. To safely update an element's priority: remove it (pq.remove(elem)), mutate its fields, and re-offer it (pq.offer(elem)).

activities.title: Self-Evaluation Checklist
checklist: I can calculate the parent and child indices for an array-backed binary heap: (i-1)>>>1, 2i+1, 2i+2
I understand why peek() is O(1) while offer() and poll() are O(log N)
I know why for-each iteration does not output elements in sorted order
I understand why PriorityQueue rejects null with NullPointerException
I understand the severe consequences of mutating elements in-place after insertion

practiceProblems.title: Kth Largest Element in a Dynamic Stream
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a class KthLargest that tracks the k-th largest element in a stream of numbers using a PriorityQueue min-heap of fixed capacity k. When a new integer is added, if the heap has fewer than k elements, offer it. If the heap has k elements and the new value is greater than peek(), poll the minimum and offer the new value. Return peek() after every addition.

testCases.input: KthLargest(3, [4, 5, 8, 2]), add(3), add(5), add(10), add(9), add(4)

practiceProblems.title: Merge N Sorted Integer Arrays
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given an array of sorted integer arrays, merge them into a single sorted array in O(N log K) time using a PriorityQueue, where K is the number of arrays and N is the total count of numbers across all arrays.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Cost to Connect Ropes
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given an array of rope lengths, connect all ropes into one rope. The cost to connect two ropes of lengths X and Y is X + Y. Find the minimum total cost to connect all ropes using a min-heap.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Meeting Rooms Required
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given an array of meeting intervals int[][] intervals where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], determine the minimum number of conference rooms required so no two meetings overlap. Sort intervals by start time and use a min-heap tracking meeting end times.

practiceProblems.title: Drain PriorityQueue to List
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a helper method drainToSortedList(PriorityQueue<T> pq) that drains all elements from the queue and returns a List<T> containing all elements strictly in ascending priority order.
